intention: Per-user charging analytics — enriched nightly charge-state fields plus true charge sessions (energy, battery before→after, efficiency) from Tesla's dx/charging/history endpoint, with a historical backfill.
request:
I'd like to start fetching nightly charging stats for vehicles. By using the same EXISTING poller as the `vehicle_data` endpoint, we can get a nightly snapshot of charging events and store them in a separate table. This would allow us to do analytics on charging behavior, energy usage, etc. etc.

Also, if there is a way to get the charging history from Tesla's API, we can backfill the table with historical data.

Wondering if this is a good idea, or if there are any gotchas with the Tesla API that would make this difficult.

I'd like to be able to query the battery level before and after charging events, as well as the energy used during the charge. This would allow us to calculate efficiency and other metrics.

Any other ideas for what to track in the charging stats table? You can do that after exploring the Tesla API and seeing what data is available.

decisions.decision: Scope = both sources: enrich nightly snapshot columns (A) AND add dx/charging/history sessions + charge_sessions table + backfill (B).
decisions.why: User selected 'Both A + B' — A is cheap (data already in JSONB), B is the only source of true per-session energy / before→after / efficiency.

decisions.decision: telemetry owns the charge_sessions table + collector + backfill; tesla owns the dx/charging/history adapter call. Multi-module → this roadmap.
decisions.why: User selected 'telemetry'; only the tesla adapter may call Tesla (boundaries). telemetry already owns nightly collection + append-only storage + the account/tesla ports.

decisions.decision: SCHEMA GATE: the charge_sessions table and the typed ChargingHistoryTesla DTO are designed ONLY after the user provides the real dx/charging/history response. No paid exploration call from the assistant.
decisions.why: User will supply the live response; Fleet API docs do not enumerate the endpoint's fields, so designing against guesses would be reworked at the DB design gate.

decisions.decision: Landed the Tier-1(a) raw exploration bootstrap (ChargingHistoryRaw + explorer surface, commit 20539b5) BEFORE authoring the RM2-tesla-add-charging-history OpenSpec change, to unblock capturing the live dx/charging/history schema.
decisions.why: Raw* explorer additions are the test-free, off-interface tesla-exploration exception (CLAUDE.md); the change's real specs (the typed capability) need the live fields this bootstrap exists to capture.

decisions.decision: Explorer run of dx/charging/history returned 403 'missing scopes'. Source B is blocked on granting vehicle_charging_cmds: (1) enable it for the app in the Tesla dev portal, (2) add it to internal/auth/oauth.go, (3) re-run cmd/setup to re-consent. This is a new prerequisite before the live schema can even be captured.
decisions.why: Tesla FAQ: 403 = token lacks required scope. Current scope is 'openid vehicle_device_data offline_access'; charging history needs vehicle_charging_cmds (charging billing/history).

decisions.decision: Added vehicle_charging_cmds to internal/auth/oauth.go inline (commit 518f129), not via a dispatched worker or formal change — a single-token enabler to unblock schema capture, parallel to D4. Fold into the Source B change later, which must ALSO add the scope to the multi-tenant web connect flow (verify in Tier 2).
decisions.why: One-token scope change; a cold-start worker is disproportionate. User confirmed the app is permitted to request the scope in the Tesla dev portal (screenshot). Awaiting user re-consent (make setup) + explorer re-run to capture the live payload.

decisions.decision: Tier 1 UNBLOCKED. The 403 was Tesla silently dropping newly-added scopes for an already-consented user; fixed by adding prompt_missing_scopes=true to the OAuth authorize URL (internal/auth/oauth.go, committed f3b95b9) alongside vehicle_charging_cmds. User re-consented and captured the live dx/charging/history payload 2026-07-15. Both D3 (schema gate) and D5/D6 (scope) are now satisfied.
decisions.why: prompt=login re-authenticates but does not re-prompt for new scopes; prompt_missing_scopes=true is Tesla's documented mechanism (Third-Party Tokens). Also fixes the multi-tenant web /connect/tesla flow, which shares auth.BuildAuthURL.

decisions.decision: dx/charging/history is Supercharger/Tesla-billed ONLY (no home/AC/third-party sessions); ChargingHistoryTesla types the FULL response (session fields + fees[] + invoices[]). Home-charging coverage is out of scope for Source B, deferred to the charging_state-transition detector (RM2 Future work).
decisions.why: Confirmed from the live payload (single Supercharger session, Medellin CO, with fees + invoice). User interview 2026-07-15: type the full response, discard nothing before telemetry (Tier 2) decides what to persist.

tiers.notes: UNBLOCKED 2026-07-15 (D7/D8): scope works via prompt_missing_scopes, live payload captured (Supercharger-only). Authoring OpenSpec artifacts (worker dispatched). DTO = full response; no DB (that is Tier 2); no miles fields -> no Km() companions.

Part (a) snapshot-column enrichment can start now. Part (b) charge_sessions BLOCKED: vehicle_charging_cmds scope now added (D6) — awaiting user re-consent + live dx/charging/history fields; then DB design gate + grill-me.
